source_title: August 6, 1997 — The day Apple and Microsoft made peace
company_context: By 1997 Apple Computer was near insolvency, losing roughly $1 billion annually with reportedly less than 90 days of cash, single-digit PC market share, and large accumulated losses. Gil Amelio had acquired NeXT (~$430 million) bringing Steve Jobs back; Jobs became interim CEO. At Macworld Boston on 6 August 1997, Apple announced Microsoft would invest $150 million, ship Office for Mac for five years, and settle patent disputes.
evidence_summary: Apple faced a liquidity crisis in 1997 with reported losses around $1 billion annually and less than 90 days of cash. The NeXT acquisition (~$430 million) returned Jobs, who became interim CEO. On 6 August 1997 Microsoft committed a $150 million investment in Apple, a five-year Office-for-Mac commitment, and a patent-dispute settlement. This stabilized Apple's finances and reputation, after which Jobs cut product lines and launched the iMac (1998), beginning one of the most documented corporate turnarounds in history.
outcome_evidence: The $150 million Microsoft investment and patent/Office settlement announced 6 August 1997 helped stabilize Apple's finances; under Jobs the company restructured its product line and returned to profitability, executing a landmark turnaround (outcome 4). The acute distress phase qualifies as cash_liquidity_crisis (outcome 3) preceding the turnaround.
source_limitations: Figures (annual losses ~$1B, <90 days cash) are widely reported and corroborated across multiple outlets but are historical estimates rather than a fetched primary 10-K line item; the $150M investment and 1997-08-06 date are well documented. Treated as B (named journalism corroborated) not A.

less than 90 days of cash reported

why_useful_for_opsiq: Classic acute cash/liquidity crisis resolved by capital injection plus disciplined refocusing, leading to a durable turnaround. Tests OpsIQ's handling of cash_liquidity_crisis severity, the role of a key-person leadership change, and re-evaluation after a strategic capital/scope decision.
